## Mains side

> **MAINS VOLTAGE. This design has NOT been safety-certified, tested or inspected by anyone.** The mains side (inlet, fuse, relay module, supply terminals, protective earth) must be wired, or checked before first power, by a person competent to do so under your local rules. The electrical verifier checks ratings and that the wires exist; it does not check creepage, enclosure, strain relief, touch protection, or any standard.

- Supply voltage declared: (115.0, 230.0) V. Mains current {'115': 5.19, '230': 2.6} A; inlet rated 10.0 A; fuse T8A (time-lag); cold-start inrush 60.0 A (the fuse riding through it was assumed, I2t not checked).
- **Set the supply's 115 / 230 V selector switch to your mains before first power** (the catalogue's note for the supply: 'set the 115/230 V selector; ring or fork terminals on mains, earth and DC wires'). 230 V on the 115 V setting destroys the supply.
- The inlet's fuse drawer and fuse-link are ordered separately from the inlet (see BOM.md).
- Live terminals that are open to touch in this open-frame design: the inlet's rear quick-connect tabs, the relay module's screw terminals and solder side, the supply's terminal block. Printed hoods in the design cover them: `mains_cover_psu`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0_washer`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nwasher`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_0_nut`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1_washer`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nwasher`, `mains_cover_psu_screw_1_nut`, `mains_cover_inlet`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_washer`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nwasher`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_0_nut`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_washer`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nwasher`, `mains_cover_inlet_screw_1_nut`. They are open where the wires enter: use fully insulated receptacles on the inlet's tabs and keep the hoods fitted whenever the machine is powered.

### Relay and neutral

The relay module switches the LIVE only and powers its own coil electronics from the mains, so the NEUTRAL is looped through its `N` terminal: one wire inlet N to relay N, a second relay N to supply N, both in one twin ferrule in the relay's N terminal. Without the neutral at the relay it never pulls in. The control board's `PS-ON` pin holds the relay in while the firmware runs and drops it on any shutdown: that relay is the only cut-off for a hotend heater whose MOSFET has failed short (report warning `cutoff_depends_on_mcu`: it does not act if the controller itself has hung).

### Protective earth

- Earth wires in the model: earth stud to supply (inlet PE to the supply's FG terminal) and earth to frame (inlet PE to the frame stud).
- Frame stud: `earth_stud`, an M5 screw into a T-nut in the outer slot of `frame_bot_left`, ring terminal and star washer under its head; scratch through the anodising under the washer (crimp M5 ring terminals: inlet PE, supply FG and bed plate each on their own lug (one conductor per tab)).
- **The model bonds ONE extrusion.** Every other frame member, the electronics tray, the inlet panel, the motors' bodies, the gantry and the bed carrier are earthed only through anodised extrusion joints, T-nuts, linear bearings or lead-screw nuts, none of which is a reliable bond. Before first power measure continuity from the inlet's earth pin to: each extrusion, the tray, the inlet panel, the supply's case, each motor body, the X beam, the bed plate. Anything above about 0.1 ohm needs its own earth wire. The bed heater is 24 V, but a mains fault to the frame must still blow the fuse.

## Declared but not drawn as wires

- `bed_probe`: its supply (5.0 V, from 'Pi 5 USB port (5 V)') is declared on the device and **not routed as a wire**: no length, no BOM quantity, no loom check for the + lead. Its 0 V return is carried in the signal cable's conductor count.
- `Y motor left`: mirror-image motor on its own driver ([stepper_y1]): invert its dir_pin (or swap one coil pair) so both turn the belts the same way

## Firmware configuration

`printer.cfg` in this folder is a copy of `out/printer_v12/electrical/printer.cfg`, generated from the electrical model and loaded by real Klipper in batch mode (klippy ran: True, ok: True, commit 29d4ec2d; that covers: klippy loads every section and plans moves on it; homing and probing against real switches are not exercised).

It holds only what the model knows. Add your host's sections (`[virtual_sdcard]`, `[pause_resume]`, `[display_status]`, macros) yourself. Firmware coordinates: X [0.0, 186.6], Y [0.0, 208.1] is the print area (set the slicer's bed origin and size to match: Y does not start at 0 because the axis has extra travel for the probe).

| [heater_bed] pid_Kp/pid_Ki/pid_Kd | pid_Kp 70.650; pid_Ki 3.388; pid_Kd 368.261 | `PID_CALIBRATE HEATER=heater_bed TARGET=60`; simulated values, heater tolerance +/-10 % not modelled |

### printer.cfg

```ini
# printer.cfg for printer_v12: GENERATED by mechloop from the electrical model. Do not edit by hand;
# change the design and regenerate. Directions (dir_pin '!') and the extruder rotation_distance must be
# confirmed on the machine; PID values come from a simulated PID_CALIBRATE and should be re-run on the real heater.
# Input shaper, pressure advance and probe offsets below are PREDICTIONS from the simulation, each resting on
# assumed values named beside it: re-measure on the machine (SHAPER_CALIBRATE, a pressure-advance test print,
# PROBE_CALIBRATE, BED_MESH_CALIBRATE).

[mcu]
# klipper_mcu: stm32f446
serial: /dev/ttyAMA0
restart_method: command

[mcu eddy]
# klipper_mcu: rp2040
# BTT Eddy Duo (RP2040), USB to the Pi 5
serial: /dev/serial/by-id/usb-Klipper_rp2040_EDDY-if00

[mcu adxl]
# klipper_mcu: rp2040
# BTT ADXL345 V2.0 (RP2040), USB to the Pi 5

[mcu host]

[printer]

full_steps_per_rotation: 400
nozzle_diameter: 0.400
filament_diameter: 1.750
heater_pin: PA2
sensor_type: ATC Semitec 104NT-4-R025H42G
sensor_pin: PF4
control: pid
pid_Kp: 47.405
pid_Ki: 19.752
pid_Kd: 28.443
min_temp: 0
max_temp: 280
max_extrude_only_distance: 100
max_extrude_only_velocity: 60
max_extrude_only_accel: 3000
# pressure advance: equal to the twin's 32 ms melt-flow lag (direct drive, 0.4 mm nozzle: factory pressure-advance values (fitted_parameters.json: extruder_lag_s), range 0.02 to 0.058 s); not measured on this machine, no sweep run: print a pressure-advance test
pressure_advance: 0.0315
pressure_advance_smooth_time: 0.04

[tmc2209 extruder]
uart_pin: PF2
run_current: 0.400
sense_resistor: 0.110

[heater_bed]
heater_pin: PA1
sensor_type: ATC Semitec 104NT-4-R025H42G
sensor_pin: PF3
control: pid
pid_Kp: 70.650
pid_Ki: 3.388
pid_Kd: 368.261
min_temp: 0
max_temp: 90
max_power: 0.95

[verify_heater extruder]
max_error: 120
check_gain_time: 20
hysteresis: 5
heating_gain: 2

[verify_heater heater_bed]
max_error: 120
check_gain_time: 60
hysteresis: 5
heating_gain: 2

[fan]
pin: PA8

# fan 'hotend_fan' is wired to the board's +5 V rail: it runs whenever the machine is powered (no firmware section)

# mains contactor ahead of the 24 V supply: switched from a host (Pi) GPIO by Moonraker, not by Klipper:
#   moonraker.conf [power printer]  type: gpio  pin: gpiochip0/gpio26
#   off_when_shutdown: True  locked_while_printing: True  restart_klipper_when_powered: True

# input shaper: predicted by the twin, not measured: resonance X 73.3 Hz, Y 61.2 Hz (belt stiffness only, no FEA frame stiffness); damping assumed. Run SHAPER_CALIBRATE
[input_shaper]
shaper_type_x: ei
shaper_freq_x: 92.6
damping_ratio_x: 0.065
shaper_type_y: mzv
shaper_freq_y: 61.6
damping_ratio_y: 0.069

# BIGTREETECH Eddy Duo on USB (HEIGHT_SENSING 5.1): mainline Klipper [probe_eddy_current]; tap for Z zero to be proven on the machine
[probe_eddy_current btt_eddy]
sensor_type: ldc1612
i2c_mcu: eddy
i2c_bus: i2c0f
x_offset: -8
y_offset: 36.146
z_offset: 2.5
speed: 5
lift_speed: 10

[temperature_probe btt_eddy]
sensor_type: Generic 3950
sensor_pin: eddy:gpio26
horizontal_move_z: 2

# ---- feedback hardware and power control (the design's el.firmware['extra_sections'])
[adxl345]
cs_pin: adxl:gpio9
spi_software_sclk_pin: adxl:gpio10
spi_software_mosi_pin: adxl:gpio11
spi_software_miso_pin: adxl:gpio12
axes_map: x,z,y

[resonance_tester]
accel_chip: adxl345
probe_points: 93.3, 104.05, 20

# BTT SFS V2.0 on the Octopus DIAG3 header (its DIAG jumper removed)
[filament_motion_sensor sfs]
switch_pin: ^PG11
detection_length: 10
extruder: extruder
pause_on_runout: True

# 24 V COB lights (overview strip + two nozzle segments) on FAN2
[output_pin lights]
pin: PD12
pwm: True
value: 0.5
shutdown_value: 0

# Quarton VLM-520-56 line laser (Class 1M): off by default, on only inside the measurement macro; PN2222A from Pi GPIO17
[output_pin nozzle_laser]
pin: host:gpio17
value: 0
shutdown_value: 0

# commissioning (owner, v11.1 plan): probe only after the bed has soaked at temperature
[gcode_macro START_PRINT]
gcode:
    {% set BED = params.BED|default(60)|float %}
    {% set SOAK = params.SOAK|default(1831)|int %}
    M190 S{BED}
    G4 P{SOAK * 1000}
    G28
    Z_TILT_ADJUST
    BED_MESH_CALIBRATE

[gcode_macro LASER_CAPTURE]
gcode:
    SET_PIN PIN=lights VALUE=0.1
    SET_PIN PIN=nozzle_laser VALUE=1
    G4 P2000
    SET_PIN PIN=nozzle_laser VALUE=0
    SET_PIN PIN=lights VALUE=0.5
```
